name: mdx-learning-loop-contract
purpose: Declare the MDx substrate that converts human intent, agent execution, durable traces, private evaluation, accountable judgment, memory, and governed adaptation into better next loops.

loop_order.description: The work the organization wants to move forward.
The retrieved institutional frame for the work.
The durable record of what happened.
The private judgment surface for whether the work improved the system.
The accountable decision that can approve, reject, revise, or override.
The changed behavior for the next loop.
The next work request shaped by promoted memory and approved adaptation.

substrate_primitives.role: Names the human or product intent and the accountable owner before work begins.
Captures the Pages, ADRs, source maps, standards, and run history used by the agent.
Records model calls, tool calls, policy decisions, diffs, approvals, refusals, cost, latency, and route proof.
Connects the work to private checks, acceptance criteria, scorecards, and risk posture.
Records the accountable human or policy decision that promotes, rejects, revises, or overrides the lesson.
Moves a lesson into Pages, decision records, generated contracts, source maps, or other MDx-owned memory.
Names the approved behavior change for model routing, fleet casting, prompt shape, work slicing, guardrails, checks, budgets, or review depth.

promotion_rule: trace is linked to an intent, context packet, execution receipt, evaluation result, and accountable judgment
adaptation names the behavior it changes and the surface that consumes the change
change is reversible or scoped behind an explicit approval boundary
source of truth is updated before generated artifacts are refreshed
local check proves the generated contract still matches the source
current_strengths: MDx already records many receipts, generated contracts, source maps, checks, and operator decisions.
Forge, Harness, fleets, Pages, Twin, Message, and Product already provide most raw ingredients for trace and evaluation.
The repo-as-truth posture supports model sovereignty because lessons can live in MDx-owned memory instead of provider behavior.

known_gaps.description: Traces and evaluations are not yet consistently promoted into changed model routing, fleet casting, checks, budgets, or review depth.
Private checks exist, but the loop still needs explicit weighting for business outcome, governance outcome, operator trust, cost, latency, and risk.
Lessons can appear in docs, generated artifacts, session notes, or Pages. The learning loop needs a single promotion lane before runtime behavior changes.
MDx should not claim reinforcement or training until real traces are intentionally captured, governed, and used by an approved training or policy process.
Lessons must survive provider swaps. Prompt-only or provider-hidden learning does not satisfy the sovereignty test.

steps: completed Forge run emits an outcome record
outcome is evaluated against private checks, acceptance criteria, cost, latency, and risk
human or policy judgment promotes or rejects the lesson
a human opens a reversible fleet casting grant over the activated lesson
next Forge casting cites the granted lesson before preferring or avoiding a runner - and only fleet casting, never model routing, budget, or review depth
blocked_authority: no budget, check policy, or review depth change
